title: SQL performance: measure the three unmeasured M0 items — per-request identity reads, sharing scope, roll-up recompute — then file what pays (epic #33631 R8/R9/R10)
body:
domain:server#5 · os-elon-musk · session_016WV4cztR1A2CZoxSZyuoGP

Filing gate: ④ child of epic #33631 (SQL performance). Item R8–R10 of the M0 ranked list (#33633): https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/issues/33631#issuecomment-6889544281 (corrected 6889939163). Maintainer's pick (seat decision card, 2026-11-15T06:44Z): 「R1 R7 R12 各一张+测量卡」.

## What is unmeasured

- **R8** per-request identity and permission resolution: a plain list is 10 statements, 2 of them data (cold ~21; `resolve-authz-context.ts` ~2406 reads the organization's member list up to 1000 rows a page). The grants cache exists and is OFF by default (`OS_AUTHZ_GRANTS_CACHE_TTL_MS=0`). Cheap on a local database; on a network database (Turso, managed PG) each is a round trip. Measure over a network.
- **R9** sharing read scope materializes `sys_record_share.record_id` (`limit: 5000`) into `id IN (…)` on every member read of a private object (`sharing-service.ts` ~747–764); hierarchy scopes expand owner ids in the app. Needs a share-seeding leg in the bench. Target shape: `id IN (SELECT record_id FROM sys_record_share WHERE …)`.
- **R10** roll-up summary recompute: per distinct parent per summary field, one aggregate + one full engine `update` on every child write (`engine-summaries-and-expansion.ts` ~458–470). Needs summary fields in the fixture.

## Output

Bench legs for all three on the M0 harness, numbers on both dialects (and over a network for R8), and a short ranked addendum on #33631. The seat files an M2 card for each item that pays. No product code in this card.

## Reader

domain:server#5 area A3 (owner of the M0 bench), next account; size M.

## Epic rules

- Name the SQL shape produced and give before/after on the M0 bench (`packages/qa/dogfood/bench/sql-perf`, PR #33662).
- Security never regresses: read scope and tenant wall stay in the pushed-down statement, with a parity test against today's path.
- A non-SQL driver keeps an in-process path it already has or refuses with a stable code (epic #33631 rules; #33626 rulings).
